// upload(name, bytes, url) sends a file to the upload server. Files over 5 MB are refused before sending.
const MAX_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024;

function checkSize(bytes) {
  if (bytes.length > MAX_BYTES) throw new Error(`file too large: ${bytes.length} bytes`);
}

async function upload(name, bytes, url = 'http://127.0.0.1:4599/upload') {
  checkSize(bytes);
  const res = await fetch(`${url}?name=${encodeURIComponent(name)}`, { method: 'POST', body: bytes });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`upload failed: ${res.status}`);
  return (await res.json()).id;
}

module.exports = { upload, checkSize, MAX_BYTES };

Both tests now pass locally, so CI shouldn't need an upload server anymore.

The failing test was calling `upload()` against the hardcoded `http://127.0.0.1:4599/upload`, where nothing listens in CI. I changed `test/upload.test.js` so the test starts its own throwaway HTTP server on a random free port. It passes that server's URL to `upload()` and shuts the server down afterwards. `upload.js` is unchanged.

The test still makes a real `fetch` call. It now also checks that the request was a `POST` to `/upload?name=a.txt` with the body `hello`. I haven't run it in CI itself, only locally.
